Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 68, verse 1–7:

Explanation of the words:

Nun: It is one of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah), written thus: نۤ, and pronounced "Nun."

And the pen and what they inscribe: That is, by the pen with which the Remembrance (al-qadr) was written, and by what they write and record.

You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman: That is, you are not, by what Allah has bestowed upon you of prophethood and what He has granted you of perfection.

A madman: That is, one possessed by madness, as the polytheists claim.

Unceasing: That is, uninterrupted; rather, it is everlasting forever.

Which of you is the afflicted one: That is, which of you is the madman.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Nun﴾: This is one of the disjointed letters, like Qaf, Sad, and Ha-Mim. Allah knows best what He intends by it. His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And the pen and what they inscribe﴾: That is, by the pen that was used to write when it was first created, and to which He said, "Write." It said, "What shall I write?" He said, "Write what will occur until the Day of Resurrection." So it ran with that. "And what they inscribe" means what the angels transcribe from the Preserved Tablet, and what the noble recording angels write of the deeds of the servants. It is an oath: Allah, exalted is He, swears by two things: the first is the pen, and the second is what is written with it, of all that He has created. The sworn matter is His saying, ﴿You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman﴾, a refutation of the polytheists who said Muhammad was mad because of what they saw of the revelation and its influence upon those whom Allah guided to faith. His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And indeed, for you is a reward unceasing﴾ falls within the oath, that is, it is part of what is sworn to: that the Prophet (ﷺ) has a reward that is never cut off, because of the good deeds he has put forward, the greatest of which is the guidance he clarified and the good ways he established, for whoever establishes a good practice has its reward and the reward of whoever acts by it until the Day of Religion. Likewise, Paradise is the reward of every good deed, and the Messenger has in it a reward that is never cut off, rather he has its highest and best part. His saying, ﴿And indeed you are upon a tremendous character﴾, is also within the scope of what is sworn to: that the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) is upon a magnificent character, that is, a great courtesy, since his Lord trained him. How then would he not be the most perfectly mannered of creation? His conduct and what was addressed to him in the Qur'an, such as "Take what is easy and enjoin what is right and turn away from the ignorant," and such as "Consult them in the matter," and such as "Had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have dispersed from around you," and other lofty courtesies with which Allah trained His Messenger, which made him the most perfect of people in manners and character. 'Aishah was asked about the character of the Prophet (ﷺ) and she said, "His character was the Qur'an." And he himself said, "My Lord trained me, and perfected my training." And he said, "I was only sent to perfect noble character."

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿So you will see and they will see which of you is the afflicted one﴾: That is, persist in what you are upon of perfection, O our Messenger, and be patient in our call. You will see after a short time, and your people who accuse you of madness will see, which of you is the afflicted one: are you the madman—far be it from you—or are they?

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of the guided﴾: In this report is consolation and solace for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that he may be patient in calling to Allah. It also contains a threat and warning to the disbelieving polytheists. That Allah is more knowing than anyone of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the guided, means that He will punish the strayer according to His practice, and He will show mercy to the guided.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues to aim at guiding the Quraysh, the people of Muhammad (ﷺ). God says: ﴿Indeed, We tested them﴾, meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh. That is, We tried and examined them with blessings and favours, so that they would be thankful, but they did not give thanks. Then We tested them with calamity and punishment, namely drought, famine and killing, so that they might repent, just as We tested the People of the Garden, and they repented. Then God mentioned the story of the People of the Garden, whom He tested, and they turned to Him and returned to obedience to Him. He says: ﴿Indeed, We tested them as We tested the people of the garden, when they swore﴾ (that is, they took an oath) ﴿that they would surely cut its fruit in the morning﴾, meaning they would cut its fruit and collect it early in the morning, before the poor could know, so that they would give them nothing. ﴿And they made no exception﴾: that is, they did not make the exception in their oath; they did not say, "if God wills." ﴿Then there passed over it a visitation from your Lord, O Our Messenger, while they were asleep﴾, which was a fire that burned it, ﴿and it became like the pitch-black night﴾, that is, the dark night, black and intensely dark. ﴿So they called out to one another in the morning﴾, meaning some of them called to others, and they were many brothers, at the beginning of the morning, saying: ﴿Go out early to your tilth﴾, if you are indeed determined to cut it this morning. ﴿So they set out, whispering to one another﴾, consulting in lowered voices, so that the poor and needy of the town would not notice them, and they agreed that ﴿no needy person shall enter it today against you﴾, as they used to enter and take from it during the lifetime of their father, may God have mercy on him. God says: ﴿And they set out early, with determined intent, able to act﴾, that is, they set out in the morning with a firm purpose, able to ensure that no needy person would enter it against them that day, but would find it and carry it to their stores, with none of the poor or needy aware of them.

God says: ﴿But when they saw it﴾, burnt, black and dark, ﴿they said﴾: "This is not our garden," ﴿Indeed, we have lost our way﴾, meaning we have lost it by going astray to it. When they realised that it was indeed their garden, but that it had burnt in the night, they retracted their first statement and said: ﴿Rather, we are deprived﴾, that is, deprived of it, because we had resolved to prevent the needy from it, though our father used to give them from it and bestow upon them out of gratitude to God and fulfilment of His right.

Here the best of them spoke, that is, the most God-fearing and the most sound in judgement, as God reports in His words: ﴿The best of them said: "Did I not tell you, 'Why do you not glorify God?'"﴾, meaning: had I not already said to you, when you said, "We will surely cut it in the morning," and you did not make the exception, that I told you: "Why do you not make the exception?" The term "glorification" (*tasbīḥ*) was applied to the exception, because glorification means declaring God free from polytheism and all other deficiencies, including incapacity. The exception likewise declares God free of that, because whoever says, "I will do it," without making the exception, has given himself a power like the power of God, who, when He says "Be," it is; He is not incapable. Thus he has associated himself with one of God's attributes. Therefore the exception is a glorification of God and a declaration of His freedom from sharing in His attributes and actions. When their brother, the wise and rightly guided one, reminded them, they said: ﴿Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers﴾, and by this acknowledgement they repented. God says: ﴿So they turned toward one another, blaming each other﴾, that is, some of them blamed others for their error in resolving to deprive the needy and for not making the exception in their oath. Among what they said was: ﴿O woe to us!﴾, that is, O our destruction, come! ﴿Indeed, we were transgressors﴾, that is, exceeding the bounds of God which He set for us, out of heedlessness and ignorance of ourselves and of what punishes the likes of us. Here, after they had turned upon themselves in blame and to God in repentance, they hoped in their Lord and did not despair of His mercy, and said: ﴿Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange something better than it. Indeed, we turn to our Lord with hope﴾. Thus they were tested with blessing and then deprived of it, and they repented. So are the disbelievers of Quraysh, who were tested with blessing and then deprived of it, going to repent as the People of the Garden repented? This story has been related only as a reminder and a lesson. Will they not then be mindful and repent? God says: ﴿Such is the punishment﴾, that is, such is this punishment, the deprivation, for whoever opposes the command of God and disobeys Him. ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew﴾. The punishment of this world has a limited time and a counted term, whereas the punishment of the Hereafter is everlasting; it does not change or pass away.

2. It is lawful to remind people of the circumstances of those who were tried and those who were spared, so that it may become a path to gratitude and patience.

3. The righteousness of parents benefits the children of believers. The People of the Garden benefited from the righteousness of their father, who used to give charity to the poor from the produce of his orchard, and the sign of their benefit was their repentance.

4. It is lawful to make the exception (*istithnāʾ*) in an oath, and it is a glorification of God, Exalted is He. Omitting it leads to sin. If he is unable to do any of these, he fasts for three days, so that this sin may be erased from his soul.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 68, verses 34–43:

Explanation of the words:

Inna lil-muttaqin (Indeed, for the God-fearing): meaning those who fear their Lord, believe in Him, affirm His oneness, and guard themselves through that against shirk (associating partners with God) and sins.

ʿInda rabbihim jannat al-naʿim (With their Lord are Gardens of Bliss): meaning that for them are Gardens of Bliss on the Day of Resurrection, with their Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

Afanajʿalu al-muslimina ka-al-mujrimin (Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals?): meaning, "Do We act unjustly in judgment and deal wrongfully, so that We make the Muslims and the criminals equal in reward, favor, and recompense?" No! The people of the Fire and the people of the Garden are not equal.

Am lakum kitabun fihi tadrusun (Or do you have a Book in which you study): meaning, you read it and thereby learned what you claim.

Inna lakum fihi lama takhayyarun (That for you therein is what you choose): meaning, you found in the Book you read that you will have therein whatever you choose.

Am lakum aymanun ʿalayna baligha (Or do you have oaths from Us, binding): meaning, do you have covenants from Us, confirmed by oaths, that We will not depart from or release you from until the Day of Resurrection?

Inna lakum lama tahkumun (That for you is whatever you decree): meaning, We have given you Our firm covenants that for you is whatever you decree for yourselves, as you wish.

Salhum ayyuhum bidhalika zaʿim (Ask them, which of them stands surety for that): meaning, ask them, O Our Messenger, about their guarantor who undertakes to them the content of the judgment they pass for themselves, namely that they will be given in the Hereafter better than what the believers are given.

Am lahum shurakaʾ (Or do they have partners): meaning, do they have partners who agree with them in what they have claimed, whom they can make responsible for what they claimed and judged for themselves, namely that they will be given better than what the believers are given on the Day of Resurrection?

Yawma yukshafu ʿan saq (The Day when a shin will be uncovered): meaning, the Day when the terror intensifies and distress grows severe, and the Lord uncovers His noble shin, which nothing resembles, when He comes to decide the judgment.

Tarhaquhum dhillah (Humiliation will cover them): meaning, humiliation will overwhelm them, what a humiliation.

Wa-qad kanu yudʿawna ila al-sujudi wa-hum salimun (And they had been called to prostration while they were sound): meaning, they had been called in the world to prayer while they were free from any ailment, yet they did not pray, refusing to prostrate out of arrogance and pride.

Meaning of the verses:

The verses were revealed in response to the polytheists who boastfully claimed that when they were resurrected on the Day of Resurrection they would be given better than what the believers are given, analogizing from their state in this world, where they were wealthy and the believers were poor. So God, Exalted, said: "Indeed, for the God-fearing with their Lord are Gardens of Bliss," meaning gardens entirely of bliss with nothing in them but that. Then, in refutation, He rebuked them for their claim, censuring and reproaching them with seven rhetorical questions of denial, the first being His saying: "Shall We treat the Muslims," those who submitted themselves to God and obeyed Him with all their limbs, "like the criminals," who committed crimes against themselves by perpetrating the greatest sins such as shirk and all other destructive acts? That is, "Do We act unjustly and wrongfully in Our judgment, so that We make the Muslims like the criminals in favor and reward on the Day of Resurrection, equalizing them?" The second is His saying: "What is wrong with you?" meaning, what has happened to you that you made this claim? The third: "How do you judge?" meaning, how did you issue this judgment? What is your proof and evidence for it? The fourth is His saying: "Or do you have a Book in which you study," meaning, do you have a book brought to you by a messenger from God, in which you read this judgment you passed for yourselves, that you will be given on the Day of Resurrection better than what the believers are given? "That for you therein is what you choose," meaning, do you have in this book whatever you choose? The answer is: No, no. The fifth is His saying: "Or do you have oaths from Us, binding until the Day of Resurrection? That for you is whatever you decree," meaning, do you have Our binding covenants, sworn by oaths from which We will not release ourselves until the Day of Resurrection, that for you is what you judged for yourselves, that you will be given better than what the believers are given? The sixth: "Ask them, which of them stands surety for that," meaning, ask them, O Our Messenger, about their guarantor who undertakes the content of the judgment they pass for themselves, that they will be given in the Hereafter better than what the believers are given. The seventh is His saying: "Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners if they are truthful." That is, do they have partners who agree with them in what they said and undertake it for them? Let them bring them if they are truthful in that. With these seven rhetorical questions of denial and rebuke, God, Exalted, negated from them everything by which they could cling to justify their false claim, both rationally and legally.

His saying, "The Day when a shin will be uncovered," means: tell them, O Our Messenger, clarifying the reality of the matter on the Day of Resurrection, so that they may be shamed by their boasting in their fallen and worthless claim. Meaning of the verses:

The verses were revealed in response to the polytheists who boastfully claimed that when they were resurrected on the Day of Resurrection they would be given better than what the believers are given, analogizing from their state in this world, where they were wealthy and the believers were poor. Then, in refutation, He rebuked them for their claim, censuring and reproaching them with seven rhetorical questions of denial, the first being His saying: "Shall We treat the Muslims," those who submitted themselves to God and obeyed Him with all their limbs, "like the criminals," who committed crimes against themselves by perpetrating the greatest sins such as shirk and all other destructive acts? They cannot, because the back of each of them becomes a single bone. "Their eyes downcast," not blinking from intense fear. 2. And do not be like the companion of the fish, Yunus son of Matta, i.e., in impatience and lack of patience, ﴿when he called out while suppressing grief﴾, i.e., filled with grief, so he said, "There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers." As for His saying, ﴿Had not a blessing from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast into the open wasteland while he was blameworthy﴾, i.e., had not God's mercy reached him, when God inspired him to repent and enabled him to do so, he would have been cast out into the open while blameworthy; but when God accepted his repentance, he was cast onto the shore of the sea while not blameworthy but praiseworthy. ﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾, i.e., chose him a second time after the first, ﴿and made him among the righteous﴾, i.e., those perfect in righteousness among the prophets and messengers. 2- It is not permissible to take a wage for conveying the call.

3- The obligation of patience in the call, whatever the hardships, so that the caller does not abandon it because of harm that befalls him.

4- Clarification of the state of the polytheists toward the Messenger (ﷺ), and what they harboured for him of hatred and envy, and the false accusations they levelled at him, such as madness, sorcery and lying.

After that severe rebuke of the polytheists who deny, which had no effect whatsoever on their souls, God Most High said to His Messenger, ﴿So leave Me with those who deny this discourse﴾, i.e., on the basis of that, leave Me with them and those who deny this discourse, and what is meant by the discourse is the Noble Qur'an. ﴿We will lead them step by step﴾, i.e., We will bring them down degree by degree, ﴿from where they do not know﴾, until it leads them to their punishment resulting from their denial and polytheism. As for His saying, ﴿And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm﴾, i.e., I will grant them time, so I do not hasten the punishment upon them; I will expand their provision and make their bodies healthy until they see that this is because of their honour with Us, and that they are better than the believers, and then We seize them. This is from My strong plan, which cannot be withstood. As for His saying, ﴿Or do you ask them for a wage, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾, i.e., rather, do you ask them for a reward for conveying the call, so that they feel the weight of a heavy load because of what they must give you as wages? Therefore they do not believe in you nor follow your call. ﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they write?﴾, i.e., the Preserved Tablet, so that they write from it what they hold and affirm? The answer is no. So be patient, O Our Messenger, for the judgment of your Lord concerning you and them, continue in your call, and let neither their denial nor their obstinacy weaken your resolve. And do not be like the companion of the fish, Yunus son of Matta, i.e., in impatience and lack of patience, ﴿when he called out while suppressing grief﴾, i.e., filled with grief, so he said, "There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers." As for His saying, ﴿Had not a blessing from his Lord reached him, he would have been cast into the open wasteland while he was blameworthy﴾, i.e., had not God's mercy reached him, when God inspired him to repent and enabled him to do so, he would have been cast out into the open while blameworthy; but when God accepted his repentance, he was cast onto the shore of the sea while not blameworthy but praiseworthy. ﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾, i.e., chose him a second time after the first, ﴿and made him among the righteous﴾, i.e., those perfect in righteousness among the prophets and messengers. The meaning of "chose him a second time" is that the first choosing was when he was a messenger to the people of Nineveh, and they opposed him, so he left them in impatience with them; he was punished, and after the punishment and reproach, He chose him again and sent him to the people of his land after that separation. God Most High said, in the sura of Yunus (al-Yaqtin): ﴿So We cast him onto the open land while he was ill, and We caused a gourd plant to grow over him, and We sent him to a hundred thousand or more, and they believed, so We gave them enjoyment for a time﴾.

As for His saying, ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the Reminder﴾, i.e., and indeed, those who disbelieve would almost throw you down through the intensity of their gaze at you, filled with rage and fury against you, ﴿when they hear the Reminder﴾, i.e., the Qur'an that we recite to them, and they say, "Indeed he is mad," out of envy of you and to turn people away from you. ﴿And it is not but a reminder to the worlds﴾, i.e., he (Muhammad ﷺ) is a reminder by which God Most High reminds mankind and the jinn; he is not mad, as the deniers and the deluded claim.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Referring matters to God when their resolution becomes difficult, for God is sufficient for that.

2- It is not permissible to take a wage for conveying the call.

3- The obligation of patience in the call, whatever the hardships, so that the caller does not abandon it because of harm that befalls him.

4- Clarification of the state of the polytheists toward the Messenger (ﷺ), and what they harboured for him of hatred and envy, and the false accusations they levelled at him, such as madness, sorcery and lying.
